title: World of Change: Shrinking Aral Sea
text: The Aral Sea was once the fourth-largest lake in the world, with an area of 68,000 square kilometers. Beginning in the 1960s, diversion of rivers for irrigation caused the lake to dry up steadily. Satellite observations from MODIS and historical sensors document the retreat of the shoreline, the emergence of the Aralkum Desert, and severe microclimate changes including hotter summers and colder winters.

title: World of Change: Antarctic Ozone Hole
text: Satellite measurements from NASA's TOMS and OMI instruments, and now OMPS, track the annual Antarctic ozone hole. Following the Montreal Protocol, long-term time series analysis reveals a statistically significant downward trend in ozone-depleting chemicals and initial signs of ozone layer healing. Seasonal cycles require analyzing the minimum October values to separate seasonal depletion from secular recovery.

title: World of Change: Arctic Sea Ice Extent
text: Sea ice extent in the Arctic reaches its minimum each September. Long-term satellite records from passive microwave sensors (SSMR and SSM/I-SSMIS) cataloged by NSIDC demonstrate a continuous downward trend of over 12% per decade since 1979. This polar amplification is directly linked to positive ice-albedo feedback, driving accelerated warming in high northern latitudes.

title: A Record-Shattering El Niño
text: The El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) creates massive warm water anomalies in the eastern equatorial Pacific. During major events like 1982-83, 1997-98, and 2015-16, rainfall anomalies along the northern coast of Peru (Piura, Tumbes) exceed several hundred percent above normal. Trend detectives must differentiate episodic ENSO variability from long-term climate signals.

title: Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2)
publisher: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO)
text: MERRA-2 is NASA's atmospheric reanalysis for the satellite era using the Goddard Earth Observing System Model (GEOS-5). It covers 1980 to the present with a native horizontal resolution of 0.5° latitude by 0.625° longitude across 72 hybrid-eta levels. MERRA-2 integrates satellite aerosol observations and advances hydrological cycle representations for global and regional trend assessments.

title: Giovanni: Earth Science Data Exploration and Analysis Tool
text: NASA Giovanni (Geospatial Interactive Online Visualization ANd aNalysis Infrastructure) is a Web-based tool for exploring vast amounts of Earth science data from NASA missions. It allows users to create time-averaged maps, generate time series plots, compute spatial correlations, and export area-averaged CSV series for missions including GPM, MODIS, AIRS, OMI, and GLDAS without downloading raw HDF/NetCDF files.

title: Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) Mission
text: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission, launched in December 2022 by NASA and CNES with CSA and UKSA partnerships, uses Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn) to measure water surface elevation across 90% of Earth's lakes, reservoirs, rivers, and oceans. SWOT provides the first global comprehensive survey of terrestrial surface water storage changes.

title: KNMI Climate Explorer: Web-based Climate Analysis System
text: The KNMI Climate Explorer is an established scientific analysis platform providing statistical testing for climate time series. It offers time series generation, detrending, seasonal cycle removal, linear regression, and non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend tests with empirical autocorrelation corrections to separate physical trends from weather noise.

title: NOAA Climate Data Online (CDO) Global Historical Weather Archive
publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
text: NOAA Climate Data Online provides quality-controlled historical observational records from in-situ surface weather stations worldwide. These ground-based measurements serve as the primary truth benchmark against which satellite reanalysis models like MERRA-2 and gridded climate datasets like NASA GISTEMP v4 calibrate surface temperature and precipitation trends.

title: Non-Parametric Trend Detection: The Mann-Kendall Test
text: The Mann-Kendall test is a rank-based non-parametric statistical method used to detect monotonic trends in environmental time series. Unlike ordinary least squares regression, it makes no assumption of normal distribution and is resilient to missing data and extreme outliers. The test statistic S counts the relative signs of all pairs; tau ranges between -1 and +1 to measure rank correlation over time.

title: Robust Estimation of Slope: The Theil-Sen Estimator
publisher: Journal of the American Statistical Association
text: The Theil-Sen estimator (Sen's slope) calculates the rate of change as the median of slopes computed between all possible pairs of sample points. With a breakdown point of approximately 29%, it provides a highly robust alternative to OLS regression in satellite observations where sensor calibration drifts or unusual extreme weather events might otherwise bias the trend slope.

title: Modified Mann-Kendall Test for Autocorrelated Environmental Series
text: Monthly Earth science time series frequently exhibit positive lag-1 autocorrelation: a warm month tends to follow another warm month. Positive autocorrelation underestimates the variance of the Mann-Kendall statistic, leading to false-positive significance. The Hamed and Rao modification calculates an effective sample size (n_eff) to adjust variance and restore accurate p-value estimation.

title: Factors Affecting the Detection of Trends in Environmental Records
publisher: Journal of Geophysical Research (Weatherhead et al. 1998)
text: The number of years required to detect a significant trend depends on the trend magnitude, the monthly variance of the noise, and the degree of autocorrelation in the residual noise. As Weatherhead et al. (1998) formulate, high natural noise requires many more decades of continuous satellite data before a trend can be confirmed with 95% statistical confidence. 'No trend yet' often simply means more data are needed.

title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate in Spatial Trend Maps
publisher: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society (Wilks 2016)
text: When performing trend tests simultaneously across dozens or hundreds of spatial grid cells, testing each at alpha = 0.05 guarantees numerous false discoveries by pure chance. Following Benjamini and Hochberg (1995) and Wilks (2016), the False Discovery Rate (FDR) control adjusts p-value thresholds so that the expected proportion of false positive cells remains strictly below q = 0.10.

title: Accounting for the Seasonal Cycle in Climate Signal Emergence
publisher: Journal of Geophysical Research (Santer et al. 2000)
text: Earth science data exhibit strong regular astronomical cycles driven by Earth's axial tilt. To detect long-term climatic change, a monthly climatology baseline is established and subtracted from each observation. These monthly anomalies isolate the secular underlying trajectory from the predictable annual oscillation.

title: Biome Profile: Tropical Rainforest (Amazon Basin & Madre de Dios)
text: Tropical rainforests are dense, humid ecosystems characterized by high constant temperatures and heavy rainfall. Deforestation and climate warming alter local hydrology: evaporation decreases as canopy cover is lost, while surface temperatures rise. In regions like the Amazon Deforestation Arc and Madre de Dios, soil wetness and dry-season precipitation provide critical indicators of degradation.

title: Biome Profile: Deserts and Arid Lands (Sechura, Atacama, Aral Basin)
text: Deserts feature severe moisture deficits where potential evapotranspiration greatly exceeds precipitation. Extreme diurnal skin temperature ranges are typical. In hyper-arid regions like the Peruvian coastal desert (Sechura, Ica), soil moisture stays near minimum thresholds except during catastrophic El Niño events that trigger ephemeral river flows and dust mobilization.

title: Biome Profile: Tidal Estuaries and Coastal River Outlets
text: Coastal and estuarine ecosystems link terrestrial drainage basins with marine environments. Remote sensing of ocean color, sea surface temperature, and precipitation runoff reveals how river plumes deliver nutrients and sediments into coastal waters. Upwelling regions along the Humboldt Current respond sharply to atmospheric shifts, making coastal stations sensitive to large-scale trends.

title: Biome Profile: Atmosphere Above Large Megacities (Urban Heat Islands)
text: Urban environments alter the atmospheric boundary layer through artificial surfaces with low albedo and high thermal mass. Skin temperature in metropolitan centers (such as Lima, Santiago, or Los Angeles) shows pronounced urban heat island (UHI) effects, while satellite sensors measure elevated tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and aerosol optical depth from vehicle and industrial emissions.

title: Biome Profile: High-Altitude Tropical Glaciers (Cordillera Blanca)
text: Tropical glaciers in the Peruvian Andes (Cordillera Blanca) represent over 70% of the world's tropical ice. Positioned at altitudes above 4,800 meters, they are exquisitely sensitive to warming freezing levels. MERRA-2 surface air temperature trends show consistent elevation-dependent warming, driving accelerated glacier shrinkage and altering dry-season water supply.

title: Tendencia
text: Cambio sostenido y continuo en el tiempo de una variable medida.

title: Trend
text: A persistent, long-term change in a measured variable over time.

title: Anomalía
text: Diferencia entre el valor de un mes y la media histórica de ese mes.

title: Anomaly
text: The difference between an observed monthly value and its historical monthly average.

title: Valor p
text: Probabilidad de observar un patrón tan marcado si no existiera una tendencia real.

title: p-value
text: The probability of obtaining a test statistic as extreme as the observed value under the null hypothesis.

title: Significancia estadística
text: Certeza matemática de que una tendencia observada no se debe a fluctuaciones aleatorias.

title: Statistical significance
text: Mathematical confidence that an observed trend is not a result of random chance.

title: Intervalo de confianza
text: Rango que contiene el verdadero valor de la pendiente con una probabilidad del 95 %.

title: Confidence interval
text: A range of values likely to contain the true trend slope with 95% probability.

title: Autocorrelación
text: Correlación entre observaciones de una serie temporal en diferentes desfases de tiempo.

title: Autocorrelation
text: Correlation of a time series with a delayed copy of itself over successive time intervals.

title: Tamaño de muestra efectivo
text: Número de observaciones estadísticamente independientes tras corregir la autocorrelación.

title: Effective sample size
text: The number of independent observations remaining after adjusting for temporal persistence.

title: Pendiente de Sen
text: Mediana de las pendientes entre todos los pares de datos; estimador robusto.

title: Sen slope
text: The median of all pairwise slopes between points, resistant to outliers.

title: Desestacionalización
text: Eliminación del ciclo anual regular para aislar el cambio de fondo.

title: Deseasonalization
text: Removal of the regular annual seasonal cycle to reveal underlying secular trends.

title: Amplificación polar
text: Fenómeno por el cual los polos se calientan más rápido que el promedio del planeta.

title: Polar amplification
text: The phenomenon where high-latitude regions warm at greater rates than lower latitudes.

title: Control FDR
text: Corrección para limitar la proporción de falsos descubrimientos al probar múltiples celdas.

title: False Discovery Rate
text: Statistical method to limit the expected proportion of false positive results across multiple tests.

title: Reanálisis atmosférico
text: Reconstrucción continua del clima combinando modelos físicos y observaciones satelitales.

title: Atmospheric reanalysis
text: A scientific reconstruction of past weather blending observations with numerical weather prediction models.

title: Albedo
text: Fracción de radiación solar reflejada por una superficie terrestre o marina.

title: Albedo
text: The proportion of incident light or radiation reflected by an Earth surface.

title: El Niño (ENSO)
text: Oscilación periódica del océano y la atmósfera en el Pacífico ecuatorial.

title: El Niño (ENSO)
text: A recurring climate pattern involving changes in equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures.

title: Detectabilidad de tendencia
text: Años de datos necesarios para separar una señal climática del ruido natural.

title: Trend detectability
text: The length of record required before a real trend becomes statistically discernible from noise.

title: Troposfera
text: Capa más baja de la atmósfera donde ocurren la mayoría de los fenómenos meteorológicos.

title: Troposphere
text: The lowest region of the atmosphere where virtually all weather takes place.

title: Profundidad óptica de aerosoles (AOD)
text: Medida de la extinción de luz solar causada por partículas suspendidas en la atmósfera.

title: Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD)
text: A measure of the extinction of direct sunlight by airborne particles (dust, smoke, pollution).

title: Temperatura de piel terrestre
text: Temperatura radiativa de la superficie física de la Tierra.

title: Skin temperature
text: The radiative temperature of the uppermost Earth surface layer.

title: Humedad de suelo
text: Fracción de agua retenida en los primeros centímetros del suelo.

title: Soil wetness
text: The fraction of moisture stored in the uppermost layer of the soil column.

title: Agua precipitable total
text: Masa total de vapor de agua contenida en una columna atmosférica vertical.

title: Precipitable water
text: The total mass of atmospheric water vapor in a vertical column from surface to space.

title: Capa de ozono
text: Concentración de ozono estratosférico que absorbe la radiación ultravioleta nociva.

title: Ozone layer
text: A region of the stratosphere that absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

title: Registro homogéneo
text: Serie temporal libre de sesgos por cambios en sensores o algoritmos de calibración.

title: Homogeneous record
text: A time series unaffected by artificial non-climatic shifts in instruments or measurement practices.

title: Tendencia monótona
text: Tendencia que se mueve en una dirección constante (creciente o decreciente).

title: Monotonic trend
text: A trend that consistently increases or decreases without reversing direction.

title: Climatología
text: Promedio multianual de las condiciones atmosféricas para cada mes del año.

title: Climatology
text: The long-term average atmospheric state for each calendar month across a baseline reference period.

title: Altimetría satelital
text: Medición de la elevación de superficies de agua mediante pulsos de radar o láser.

title: Satellite altimetry
text: The measurement of surface elevation of oceans and lakes using radar or laser pulses from orbit.
